purpose: Assemble one dependency-free offline tactical browser arena from a closed game specification, deterministic session state machine, generated PNG and WAV assets, inspectable HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and exact project validation.

properties.path: target project directory outside the protected live machine body

relationships: compiles a closed ready-playing-paused-won-lost session graph and embeds the exact normalized graph into the game source
generates and consumes local PNG and WAV assets without a network, package manager, framework, or cloud provider
retains browser execution, visual quality, controls, audio playback, accessibility, and gameplay balance as separate host-evidence questions

anatomy_refs.basis: Emits a bounded requestAnimationFrame update/draw loop with explicit delta clamping and terminal session states.
Emits explicit movement, projectile, damage, reload, reward, win, and loss rules bound to the normalized game specification.
Emits keyboard, pointer, and touch mappings for movement, aiming, firing, reload, pause, start, and reset.
Emits a responsive HUD for selected target health, tower health, credits, ammunition, session state, and explicit controls.
Compiles and embeds the existing closed deterministic state-machine grammar as the session control graph.

limitations: the current schema builds one bounded 2D tower-defense arena shape rather than arbitrary game genres, engines, networking, physics, saves, user accounts, or downloadable native executables
source and assets are generated and structurally validated but JavaScript is not executed by the deterministic core
browser rendering, input behavior, audio permission/playback, frame pacing, responsive layout, accessibility, fun, and balance require later browser, user, or authorized host evidence
maximum enemy count is 64 and the project intentionally has no third-party runtime dependencies

truth.basis: The exact game and state specifications, source/assets, digests, static checks, and absent browser observation remain distinguishable.

agency.basis: The caller supplies the complete bounded arena specification, output path, extra checks, and replacement choice; the generated game never calls a service or grants itself host authority.

continuity.basis: The mixed project is staged, validated, published, and revalidated with rollback, and its explicit JSON sources make later extension inspectable.

wisdom-before-speed.basis: Closed schemas, bounds, deterministic state compilation, generated container checks, local-reference checks, and exact digest checks precede publication.
